close_reason: Replaced all .expect() in library code; ser() helper added to helpers.rs; list paths use collect::<Result>()?, individual inserts use unwrap_or_else
description: CLAUDE.md states: 'No .unwrap() or .expect() in library code — propagate with ?'. The handlers contain ~20 .expect("type derives Serialize and is always serializable") calls (email.rs, mailbox.rs, identity.rs, submission.rs, vacation.rs, thread.rs, etc.) for serde_json::to_value(&set_err) and similar. In practice these cannot fail (the types derive Serialize without custom impls and have string-compatible map keys), but they violate the stated policy and set a precedent for contributors to add more. The correct fix is to either: (a) use map_err and propagate, or (b) define a newtype that serializes via hardcoded JSON so the conversion is infallible by construction.
title: .expect() calls in library code violate project no-expect policy
